course: CMU 21-254: Linear Algebra and Vector Calculus for Engineers
title: Bases, Dimension, Column Space, and Null Space
audience: SI leader teaching live on a whiteboard. This is not a student worksheet.
toneRule: Keep explanations very simple, verbal, and board-friendly. Avoid textbook phrasing unless the problem needs it.
sessionGoal: Students should be able to find bases for column spaces and null spaces, use pivot columns correctly, and explain dimension using rank and nullity.
quickStartIfUnprepared: Write: basis = spanning set with no redundancy.
Write: rank = number of pivots, nullity = number of free variables.
Emphasize: for \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\), use pivot columns from the original \(A\), not the RREF columns.
Do Problem 1 slowly. It is the most important one.
If time is short, do Problem 1 and Problem 3.
sayThisFirst: A basis is a clean, non-redundant way to describe a space.
Dimension means how many basis vectors you need.
For a column space basis, find the pivot columns in RREF, then go back to the original matrix.
boardPlan: At the top, write: basis = span + independent.
Write the rank-nullity formula: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{nullity}(A)=\) number of columns of \(A\).
Explain that RREF is for finding pivots and equations, but original columns are used for \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\).
Use Problem 1 to find \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\), \(\operatorname{Nul}(A)\), rank, and nullity from one matrix.
Use Problem 2 to show coordinates in a basis.
Use Problem 3 to show a subspace basis from equations.

keyFormulas.name: Basis
keyFormulas.latex: \text{a spanning set with no redundant vectors}
keyFormulas.plainEnglish: A basis describes a space with the fewest clean directions.

keyFormulas.name: Dimension
keyFormulas.latex: \dim(V)=\text{number of vectors in a basis for }V
keyFormulas.plainEnglish: Dimension is the number of independent directions.

keyFormulas.name: Rank-nullity
keyFormulas.plainEnglish: For an m by n matrix, pivots plus free variables equals the number of columns.

keyFormulas.name: Column space basis
keyFormulas.latex: \text{Use pivot columns of the original matrix }A.
keyFormulas.plainEnglish: Do not use the RREF columns as the final column-space basis.

commonMistakes: Using columns of RREF as a basis for \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\). Use pivot columns from the original \(A\).
Forgetting that null space vectors have one entry for each column of A.
Confusing rank with the number of rows.
Confusing nullity with the number of zero rows.
Calling a spanning set a basis before checking redundancy.
notationWarnings: For null space, solve Ax=0, not Ax=b.
For coordinates in a basis B, write [v]_B to show these are coordinates, not the standard vector.

problems.title: Column space and null space from RREF
problems.studentPromptLatex:
Let
\[A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2&-1\\2&1&5&0\\0&1&1&2\\1&-1&1&-3\end{bmatrix},\qquad \operatorname{rref}(A)=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2&-1\\0&1&1&2\\0&0&0&0\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}.\]
Find a basis for \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\), a basis for \(\operatorname{Nul}(A)\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A)\), and \(\operatorname{nullity}(A)\).
problems.whatToSayBefore: Tell students: the RREF tells us where the pivots are. But the column-space basis comes from the original matrix.

drawInstructions: Draw the RREF matrix and circle the pivots in columns 1 and 2.
Put a box around columns 1 and 2 of the original matrix A.
Write x_3=s and x_4=t to show where the null-space parameters come from.
Draw a simple split: pivot columns describe \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\), free variables describe \(\operatorname{Nul}(A)\).

walkthrough.label: Find pivot columns
walkthrough.latex: Pivots are in columns 1 and 2, so use columns 1 and 2 of the original \(A\).

walkthrough.label: Solve Ax=0 using the RREF
walkthrough.latex:
The RREF gives
\[x_1+2x_3-x_4=0,\qquad x_2+x_3+2x_4=0.\]
Let \(x_3=s\) and \(x_4=t\). Then \(x_1=-2s+t\) and \(x_2=-s-2t\).

walkthrough.label: Rank and nullity
walkthrough.latex: There are 2 pivots, so \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=2\). There are 2 free variables, so \(\operatorname{nullity}(A)=2\). Check: \(2+2=4\), the number of columns.

commonMistakes: Using columns 1 and 2 of the RREF as the \(\operatorname{Col}(A)\) basis instead of the original \(A\).
Forgetting that the null-space basis vectors must have 4 entries.
Calling the zero rows the nullity. Nullity is the number of free variables.

practiceLabPointer.note: More practice with column space, null space, bases, and dimensions.

problems.title: Coordinates in a nonstandard basis
problems.studentPromptLatex:
Let \(B=\{b_1,b_2,b_3\}\) where
\[b_1=\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{bmatrix},\quad b_2=\begin{bmatrix}2\\0\\1\end{bmatrix},\quad b_3=\begin{bmatrix}0\\3\\-1\end{bmatrix}.\]
Decide whether \(B\) is a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^3\). Then find \([v]_B\) for \(v=\begin{bmatrix}5\\-1\\3\end{bmatrix}\).
problems.whatToSayBefore: Tell students: coordinates in B are not the same as standard coordinates. We are solving for the weights on the basis vectors.

drawInstructions: Draw three independent directions from the origin labeled \(b_1, b_2, b_3\).
Draw v as a target vector.
Emphasize that [v]_B is the list of coefficients, not the same drawing as v.

walkthrough.label: Build the basis matrix
walkthrough.latex:
Put the basis vectors as columns:
\[P=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\1&0&3\\0&1&-1\end{bmatrix}.\]

walkthrough.label: Check if B is a basis
walkthrough.latex:
\[\det(P)=-1\neq 0.\]
So the columns are independent and span \(\mathbb{R}^3\). Therefore \(B\) is a basis.

walkthrough.label: Solve for coordinates
walkthrough.latex:
We solve \(P[v]_B=v\), or
\[c_1b_1+c_2b_2+c_3b_3=v.\]
The solution is
\[[v]_B=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\3\\0\end{bmatrix}.\]

commonMistakes: Forgetting to put basis vectors as columns.
Thinking [v]_B means the same thing as v.
Stopping after det is nonzero and forgetting to find the coordinate vector.

practiceLabPointer.note: Good follow-up for basis and coordinate practice.

problems.title: Basis and dimension of a solution subspace
problems.studentPromptLatex:
Let
\[W=\{(x,y,z,w)\in\mathbb{R}^4: x+y-z=0,\; 2x+y+w=0\}.\]
Find a basis for \(W\) and find \(\dim(W)\).
problems.whatToSayBefore: Tell students: this is a homogeneous system, so the solution set is a subspace. Then we parametrize it.

drawInstructions: Do not try to draw \(\mathbb{R}^4\) exactly.
Draw a small parameter table with x=s and y=t.
Show that z and w are controlled by s and t.
Say this subspace has two independent directions, so dimension 2.

walkthrough.label: Use the equations to solve for z and w
walkthrough.latex: From \(x+y-z=0\), we get \(z=x+y\). From \(2x+y+w=0\), we get \(w=-2x-y\).

walkthrough.label: Read the basis and dimension
walkthrough.latex:
A basis is
\[\{(1,0,1,-2),(0,1,1,-1)\}.\]
There are two basis vectors, so \(\dim(W)=2\).

commonMistakes: Trying to draw \(\mathbb{R}^4\) literally instead of using parameters.
Forgetting that the vector has four components.
Not checking that the equations are homogeneous before calling it a subspace.

What is the difference between v and [v]_B?

open.title: The fewest directions that still get you everywhere
say: Last time: span is where you can reach, independence means nothing is wasted. Put them together and you get a basis: enough directions to reach everything, with no extras.
The number of vectors in a basis is the dimension. A line has dimension 1, a plane 2, space 3.

ask.q: Give me a basis for the xy-plane. Now give me a different one.
ask.a: {(1, 0), (0, 1)} works; so does {(1, 1), (1, −1)}, or any two non-parallel vectors.

write: \(\dim V=\#\text{ vectors in any basis of }V\)

idea.title: Two spaces live inside every matrix
say: Every matrix A has a column space: all the outputs Ax you can produce. It's the span of A's columns.
And a null space: all the inputs that A crushes to zero.

RREF finds both, but there's a trap: RREF tells you which columns are pivot columns, and then you go back and take those columns from the original A. Row operations change the column space; they keep the null space.
draw: Draw A on the left and RREF(A) on the right with an arrow labeled 'row ops'.
Circle the pivots in the RREF, then draw arrows back to the same column numbers in A: 'Col(A) basis comes from here'.
Under the RREF write: free variables → Nul(A).

ask.q: Why can't we use the RREF's columns for Col(A)?
ask.a: Row operations change the columns themselves, so the RREF's columns usually span a different space. They only tell us which original columns to keep.

ask.q: What stays the same under row operations?
ask.a: The solutions of Ax = 0, so the null space.

launch.say: From this one matrix and its RREF, find a basis for Col(A), a basis for Nul(A), the rank and the nullity.
circulate: Who used RREF columns for Col(A)? Have them compare with A's original columns.
Check that null-space vectors have 4 entries.

askFirst.q: Where are the pivots, and which variables are free?
askFirst.a: Pivots in columns 1 and 2; x₃ and x₄ are free.

steps.say: Pivots are in columns 1 and 2 of the RREF. So the pivot columns of A are A's own first two columns.

ask.q: What happened to columns 3 and 4 of A?
ask.a: They're combinations of columns 1 and 2, so they add nothing to the span.

steps.say: Col(A) basis: (1, 2, 0, 1) and (0, 1, 1, −1), straight from A.
steps.why: The column space lives in ℝ⁴ (4 rows), even though it's only a plane in there.

steps.say: Now Nul(A). From the RREF: x₁ + 2x₃ − x₄ = 0 and x₂ + x₃ + 2x₄ = 0. Let x₃ = s and x₄ = t.
Split the general vector by parameter: s(−2, −1, 1, 0) + t(1, −2, 0, 1).

ask.q: How do you know these two are independent without computing?
ask.a: Look at positions 3 and 4: one vector has (1, 0) there and the other has (0, 1). Neither can be a multiple of the other.

steps.say: Two pivots: rank 2. Two free variables: nullity 2. 2 + 2 = 4 columns. ✓

ask.q: If A had 4 pivots instead, what would the null space be?

si06-p1.meaning: A takes ℝ⁴ and squeezes it: a two-dimensional null space gets crushed to zero, and the outputs fill only a two-dimensional plane inside ℝ⁴. Rank + nullity = 4 is the bookkeeping: every input dimension is either kept or crushed.

ifStuck.if: a student gives RREF columns for Col(A)
ifStuck.then: check whether (1, 0, 0, 0), the RREF's first column, is a combination of A's columns. Here it isn't.

si06-p1.transition: A basis gives every vector a unique recipe. Next problem: find the recipe, meaning the coordinates, in a nonstandard basis.

launch.say: Is B a basis for ℝ³? If so, find the coordinates of v in B: the recipe for v using b₁, b₂, b₃.
circulate: Check that the basis vectors go in as columns.
Who stops after the determinant? The coordinates are still needed.

askFirst.a: The coefficients c₁, c₂, c₃ with v = c₁b₁ + c₂b₂ + c₃b₃.

steps.say: Put b₁, b₂, b₃ in as columns of P.

ask.q: What does P times a coordinate vector give?

steps.say: det P = −1, not zero, so the columns are independent and span ℝ³. B is a basis.

ask.q: Why is 'independent' enough here, without checking span separately?
ask.a: Three independent vectors in ℝ³ automatically span ℝ³.

steps.say: Solve P c = v. You get c = (−1, 3, 0).

ask.a: v can be built from b₁ and b₂ alone.
No: the first is v in standard coordinates, the second is its recipe in basis B.

si06-p2.meaning: The same arrow v gets a different address depending on the basis. In the standard basis it's (5, −1, 3); in B it's (−1, 3, 0): one step backwards along b₁, three steps along b₂.

ifStuck.if: a student thinks [v]_B is just v
ifStuck.then: compute −1b₁ + 3b₂ + 0b₃ with them and compare to (−1, 3, 0).

si06-p2.transition: Last one: a subspace given by equations. Find a basis and count.

launch.say: W is cut out by two equations in ℝ⁴. Find a basis for W and its dimension.
circulate: Nobody needs to draw ℝ⁴. Parametrize instead.
Check every basis vector has 4 components.

askFirst.q: How do you know W is a subspace before doing anything?
askFirst.a: Both equations are homogeneous and linear.

steps.say: Solve each equation for one variable: z = x + y and w = −2x − y.

ask.q: Which variables are we treating as free?
ask.a: x and y; z and w are determined by them.

steps.say: Let x = s, y = t. Then every vector in W is (s, t, s + t, −2s − t).

ask.q: How many free parameters? What does that predict?

steps.say: Those two vectors are a basis, so dim W = 2.

ask.q: Connect to rank-nullity: what matrix is W the null space of?
ask.a: The 2 × 4 coefficient matrix. It has rank 2, so nullity = 4 − 2 = 2.

steps.why: Two independent equations in four unknowns always leave a two-dimensional solution space.

si06-p3.meaning: Each independent equation cuts one dimension away. ℝ⁴ has 4 dimensions and two equations remove two, leaving a two-dimensional flat slice.

ifStuck.then: ask how many variables W's vectors have: x, y, z, w.

wrap.write: Col(A): pivot columns of the ORIGINAL A. Nul(A): parametrize the free variables. rank + nullity = # columns.

exit.q: For Col(A), do we use the original matrix or the RREF columns?
exit.a: The original matrix; RREF only tells us which columns are pivots.

exit.q: What's the difference between v and [v]_B?
exit.a: v is the vector; [v]_B is its list of coefficients in basis B.

exit.q: Two independent homogeneous equations in ℝ⁵. What's the dimension of the solution space?
